summary: A federal judge paused the FCC’s early review of eight ABC stations. The Army said it finished disposing of unstable explosives in Iowa, while Governor-elect Rob Sand challenged the handling of the operation. Treasury extended some financial reporting deadlines after its financial crimes office took systems offline. Jamieson Greer formally proposed tariffs on 14 economies, and a consortium including a U.S. government lender signed a deal for Lukoil’s overseas assets. Vice President JD Vance defended Nvidia’s role in competition with China and played down the prospect of a pardon for Jensen Huang as lawmakers called for oversight. Open items include the reported shelving of U.S.–Russia business proposals, Huang and Teter congressional appearances, Iran’s claim of three tanker mine strikes, White House contractor order and congressional responses, the reported breach of an unclassified CIA system, the reported continuation of Huang’s security clearance, separate signed Alaska election certification, Massie’s Epstein records bill and Drew Lynch’s response. Coverage of the Fed, Venezuela, immigration litigation, Iran funding and candidate organizing was limited. Representative Jimmy Gomez’s announced December 1 resignation and Mississippi election disputes remain on the House and election watch.
scope: Focused Thanksgiving review of court rulings, federal service interruptions, trade proposals, congressional oversight and reactions to Nvidia leadership. Election certification, active court dockets, Iran funding, Venezuela’s election timetable and nomination organizing received limited checks.
